findings: Multiple-comparisons risk: per-symbol H1 family/hour/entry-geometry coordinate search across 94 'independent' symbols is a large parameter search per symbol. Even with true statistical independence between symbols, each symbol's own search inflates false-positive risk for hitting an 80% win-rate / positive-expectancy target by chance. No minimum trade-count or search-complexity cap is specified, so a symbol could clear the bar on too few trades to be meaningful.

FINAL window too short for the claim size: 'early-August onward' as untouched FINAL, evaluated as of 2026-08-25, gives roughly 3-4 weeks of OOS data. That is not enough eligible-day executions (1..3/day) per symbol across 94 symbols to support an 80% win-rate + positive-expectancy claim with statistical confidence — sample sizes per symbol will likely be single digits to low double digits.

Contamination risk from prior evidence: V64/V69/V73 are explicitly 'EXPOSED DEVELOPMENT, NOT UNTOUCHED OOS' through 2026-07-31. Using them as a 'bounded hypothesis seed' is acceptable only if there is a hard, auditable boundary preventing any parameter, threshold, or geometry choice derived from that exposure from leaking into what counts as FINAL — this boundary/mechanism is not described (no versioned parameter freeze date, no hash-lock of the DEV config before FINAL starts).

No stated reconciliation mechanism for eligible-day counting. The forbidden list calls out 'silent eligible-day deletion' but the plan doesn't describe an audit trail (e.g., total calendar days vs. eligible days vs. executed days per symbol, published and diffable) that would actually catch silent deletion if it happened.

No explicit survivorship-bias control for the 94-symbol universe. With independent per-symbol optimization, some symbols will fail to meet the 80%/positive-expectancy bar by chance alone. The plan must pre-register what happens to failing symbols (they must remain reported as failures, not dropped/excluded from the aggregate 'how many symbols worked' picture) — this rule is not stated.

Data integrity checks are named (OKX-first with continuity-checked crypto fallbacks, Twelve Data M5 for forex) but the actual continuity/fallback validation method isn't specified — e.g., how gaps, provider disagreements, or M5→H1 aggregation edge cases (weekend rollovers, session boundaries) are detected and logged rather than silently smoothed over.

Deterministic replay is asserted as the performance-truth mechanism but no artifact-locking method is described (e.g., content-hash of the exact data snapshot + code version + parameter set per symbol run) that would let an independent reviewer actually reproduce a claimed result bit-for-bit.
review.proposal: Approve only a DEV/VALIDATION-scoped continuation with these bounded refinements before any FINAL claim is made: (1) Freeze and hash-lock the per-symbol search space (H1 family, hour set, entry-geometry parameters, SL rule) at end of DEV, before touching VALIDATION or FINAL data, and record the hash alongside results. (2) Require a minimum trade count per symbol (propose n>=20-30 eligible-day executions) before any win-rate/expectancy figure for that symbol is reported as anything other than 'insufficient sample.' (3) Extend or clearly label the FINAL window's statistical power — either wait for more elapsed untouched time before claiming pass/fail per symbol, or report results as provisional with explicit confidence intervals. (4) Publish a per-symbol eligible-day reconciliation table (calendar days / eligible days / executed days / reason codes for any excluded day) so silent deletion is mechanically detectable by any of the five reviewing providers. (5) Pre-register the survivorship rule: all 94 symbols must appear in the final report regardless of outcome, with failing symbols shown, not filtered. (6) Document the exact continuity-check logic for OKX crypto fallbacks and Twelve Data M5-to-H1 aggregation, including how boundary/gap cases are logged rather than interpolated silently. (7) Attach a deterministic-replay manifest (data snapshot hash, code commit, parameter hash) to any result before it can be cited as evidence in future rounds — no performance number should circulate without this attached.

findings: The contract correctly requires independent per-symbol research, exact-instrument data, 1–3 eligible-day executions, RR restricted to {1,2}, at least 80% win rate, positive expectancy, and conservative same-bar stop-loss handling.
V64/V69/V73 are exposed development evidence and may only seed bounded hypotheses; they cannot support out-of-sample or performance claims.
The early-August boundary is valid only if all legacy-prior knowledge ends on 2026-07-31 and no post-boundary data, metadata, fallback selection, or aggregate result influences research choices.
Continuity-checked crypto fallbacks create integrity risk unless provider choice, timestamp normalization, duplicate removal, gaps, and splice boundaries are fixed before outcome evaluation.
A coordinate search over family, hour, and entry geometry can overfit small per-symbol samples even without leakage; complexity and trial counts must be bounded in advance.

The 80% win-rate and positive-expectancy constraints require deterministic treatment of fees, spread, slippage, ambiguous intrabar ordering, missing bars, eligibility, and zero-trade or low-sample cases.

Per-symbol independence prohibits pooled parameter selection, cross-symbol eligibility rules learned from outcomes, symbol deletion after weak results, and portfolio-level tuning that indirectly transfers FINAL information.
review.proposal: Before replay, freeze a versioned 94-symbol manifest, exact instrument identifiers, provider precedence, retrieval timestamps, raw-data hashes, timezone/session rules, continuity thresholds, corporate-action or contract-mapping rules, and deterministic gap/duplicate policies. Define immutable DEV, VALIDATION, and FINAL date ranges; keep FINAL inaccessible until every symbol's hypothesis family, search bounds, tie-breaker, eligibility logic, cost model, and minimum sample requirement are frozen. On DEV only, run a finite predeclared grid for H1 family/hour/entry geometry and RR in {1,2}; select independently per symbol using a deterministic objective that first enforces positive expectancy and minimum sample sufficiency, then applies stability and simplicity tie-breakers. Use VALIDATION only for accept/reject or one predeclared bounded refinement cycle, never iterative tuning. Log every calendar day with eligible, ineligible, missing-data, and execution counts so silent eligible-day deletion is detectable; enforce 1–3 executions on each eligible day. Resolve same-bar TP/SL ambiguity against the strategy, and include deterministic spread, fees, and slippage. Seal configurations and hashes before one untouched FINAL replay beginning after 2026-07-31. Report every symbol, including failures and zero-trade cases, with no deletion or pooling. Make performance claims only from the sealed deterministic replay and label DEV/VALIDATION results as research evidence.
